title: Website launch: readiness and cutover
summary: Check SEO, transactions, tracking, DNS and recovery before launch.
why: A launch is a system change; one missing dependency can interrupt traffic, transactions or data.
Clear go/no-go and recovery conditions help the team decide quickly.
know: Cover functionality, content, SEO, measurement, privacy, DNS/TLS, performance, backups and ownership.
Inventory existing GA4/GSC first. Activate Ads/Meta for planned channels; check titles, descriptions and Open Graph separately.
Production needs its own checks for indexing, forms, payments and tracking even if preview worked.
inputs: Approved version, domain, release window, decision owner and operations contacts
Acceptance, redirects, events, DNS, backup and recovery plans
actions: Build the go/no-go checklist; verify staging paths, SEO, tracking and required policies.
Inspect production DNS/TLS/email, sync, environment variables and monitoring; prepare a recoverable version.
Cut over within existing authorization. Remove production noindex or password restrictions only where appropriate.
Check representative URLs, orders/forms, events and GSC. Deliver a dated, versioned release record and monitoring plan.
done: Production tasks work, old URLs map correctly and analytics events deduplicate.
No unintended staging restrictions remain; ownership is handed over and failed items have decisions.
pitfalls: Removing protection from admin or preview content with the public site.
decision: Use acceptance results to decide whether to launch and who can pause or recover.

reader.concept: Launch moves an accepted version into production and verifies continuity for users, search engines and operations.
reader.when: Use this for a new site, redesign cutover or launch decision.

example.situation: A preview form works, but production lacks its receiving configuration.
example.lesson: Recheck at the production URL after switching.

reader.first_step: Mark required items passed, failed or awaiting a decision.
